# Collection#splice(0, count, items) empties the collection, and a TreeStore replace-all hits it since #20213

## Context

`Collection#splice(0, count, toAddArray)` removes everything and adds `toAddArray` in one call. Instead of leaving exactly the added items, it ends empty: `count` is 0 and the added items land in `removedItems`. Julia captured this as a defect-note while reviewing #20213.

Since #20213 (merged as `7e026ef22d`), `TreeStore#splice()` hands a full removal to the Collection in this numeric form, so a tree replace-all hits the defect too. A probe in Node, Turbo Mode:

```js
const store = Neo.create(TreeStore, {model, data: [{id: 'a'}, {id: 'b'}]});

store.splice(0, store.getCount(), [{id: 'x'}, {id: 'y'}]);
store.getCount() // 0 on dev 5798ef6199; 2 on 4de3f3cda8, before #20213
```

## The Problem

The full-clear optimization in `Collection#splice()` (`src/collection/Base.mjs`, "Optimization: If this is a full clear operation") replaces the array without updating the method's local reference:

```js
removedItems = items;
me._items    = [];
```

The add path below still works on the local `items`, which is now the removed array:
- below the large-array threshold, `items.splice(finalIndex, 0, ...addedItems)` inserts the new items into `removedItems` and leaves `me._items` empty;
- above it, `me._items = beginning.concat(addedItems, end)` rebuilds from the removed array, so the removed items come back.

A plain `Collection` or `Store` has had this since the optimization landed. #20213 made it reachable through `TreeStore`'s replace-all as well.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Collection#splice()` caches `items = me._items` on entry. Every branch except this one mutates that same array in place, which is why only the full clear leaves the reference stale.
- The add path reads `items` to choose between assigning `addedItems` (an empty collection) and inserting into the existing array.
- `TreeStore#splice()` step 4 has delegated `super.splice(0, me.count, visibleToAdd, silent)` for a full removal since #20213. A clear passes no additions; a replace-all passes its visible new nodes.

## The Fix

In the full-clear branch, point the local reference at the new array as well: `items = me._items = []`. The add path then sees an empty collection and assigns `addedItems`. No change in `TreeStore`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `Collection#splice(0, count, items)` leaves exactly `items`, in order, with a matching `count`, and reports the old items as `removedItems`. A spec pins it below the large-array threshold, and above it if one applies.
- [ ] AC-2: A `TreeStore` replace-all, `splice(0, count, newNodes)`, keeps its new nodes. A spec arm in `TreeStoreClear.spec.mjs` pins it.
- [ ] AC-3: `clear()` still resolves no node position by scanning; the existing `TreeStoreClear.spec.mjs` arms pass.
- [ ] AC-4: The unit tier passes.

## Out of Scope

- The per-item cost of the Collection's array removal, already out of scope in #20212.

## Related

- #20212 / #20213: the TreeStore change that made the defect reachable through a tree replace-all.
